- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast slightly to account for bearish momentum.
- Model often overshoots after sharp spikes in sentiment or price; apply a 10–20% downward correction to forecasts following spikes.
- Forecasting horizon 30d shows persistent underestimation of late-period values; add a 5–10% upward bias for days 25–30 if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30d forecasts: model often fails to capture price returning to historical mean after volatility; apply a smoothing filter or adjust for recent mean.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lead time adjustment for price reversals.
- High sentiment + high forecast = high error; if sentiment >0.7 and forecast >1.5, apply a 15–25% downward correction to avoid overconfidence bias.
